Rashi on Nedarim 13a:10:1.english: Who is [the Sage of whom] we have heard, for whom there is no difference between "a lamb," "for a lamb," [and] "like a lamb" - [Meaning] that [in] all of them, [when one says] "that I eat of yours," it is forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:10:2.hebrew: ר"מ היא - דפליג עליה דר"י, דאי ר"י, לית ליה "אימרא", דאמר: האומר "ירושלים" לא אמר כלום:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:10:2.english: It is Rabbi Meir - Who disagrees with Rabbi Yehuda; for if [it were] Rabbi Yehuda, he does not accept [the expression] "imra" [a lamb], as he says: One who says "Jerusalem" has said nothing.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:11:1.english: And [with regard to] all of them, [if he says,] “I will not eat of yours,” [they are] permitted - Even if he said, “For a lamb, I will not eat of yours.”

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:11:2.english: Who have we heard for whom there is no difference between “a lamb,” “for a lamb,” [and] “like a lamb” - That [with regard to] all of them, [when he says,] “that I eat of yours,” it is prohibited.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:11:3.english: And [with regard to] all of them, "I will not eat of yours," [it is] permitted - Even if he said, "For a lamb, I will not eat of yours."

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:12:1.hebrew: לא קשיא הא דאמר לאימרא - מתני' דתנן לקמן וכו', דאמר "לאימרא לא אוכל לך", דהיינו לקרבן, דמשמע: לקרבן יהא, לפיכך לא אוכל לך. וברייתא דקתני מותר, תריץ לה הכי: דאמר "לא לאימרא לא אוכל לך" — הא אם אוכל לך, יהא כאימרא, דהיינו מכלל לאו הן; ולהכי מותר, דלר"מ לית ליה מכלל לאו [הן]:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:12:1.english: This is not difficult; that is where he said, "For a lamb" - [This refers to] the mishna that we learned below, etc., where he said, "For a lamb, I will not eat from you" — which means "for a sacrifice," implying: it shall be for a sacrifice, therefore I will not eat from you. And the baraita that teaches [that he is] permitted, resolve it thus: that he said, "Not for a lamb, I will not eat from you" — implying that if I do eat from you, it shall be like a lamb, which is [inferring] a positive from a negative; and therefore [he is] permitted, for according to Rabbi Meir, one does not [infer] a positive from a negative.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:13:1.hebrew: האומר עולה - יהא שאוכל לך, או מנחה כו', אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:13:1.english: One who says: A burnt-offering - [i.e., "Let] that which I eat of yours be [a burnt-offering]," or "a meal-offering," etc., [it is] forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:13:2.english: Rabbi Yehuda renders [it] permitted - Because he did not say "like a burnt-offering" [or] "like a sin-offering."

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:14:1.hebrew: סתמא תנא כרבי מאיר דלא שאני ליה בין אימרא לאימרא - דאסר היכא דאמר ירושלים כמאן דאמר כירושלים, ולהכי אסור היכא דאמר קרבן כהיכא דאמר כקרבן:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:14:1.english: [This] unattributed [mishna] was taught in accordance with Rabbi Meir, for whom there is no difference between imra [a lamb] and le'imra [as a lamb] - For he prohibits where one says "Jerusalem" just as where one says "like Jerusalem," and therefore it is prohibited where one says "an offering" just as where one says "like an offering."

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:15:1.english: If it is Rabbi Meir - [This refers to] the first clause [of the Mishnah], which teaches: "The offering that I will eat of yours" — [it is] forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:15:2.english: And isn't it taught [in a baraita]: The Sages concede to Rabbi Yehuda - That is, Rabbi Meir, who disagrees with him.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:15:3.hebrew: שלא נדר זה אלא בחיי קרבן - דכי אמר הא קרבן שאוכל לך, משמע כמאן דאמר חיי קרבן שאוכל לך, ולא כלום קאמר:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:15:3.english: For this [person] only vowed by the life of an offering - For when he says, "This offering [ha korban] that I will eat of yours," it sounds like one who says, "[By] the life of an offering [that] I will eat of yours," and he has said nothing [binding].

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:1:1.hebrew: ואמר זה כזה - ובהא קא מיפלגי, מר סבר בעיקרו מתפיס, ומר סבר בהיתר קא מתפיס לאחר זריקת דמים:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:1:1.english: And he said: This [is] like that - And it is regarding this that they disagree: one master holds [that] he is associating [the vow] with its original [forbidden state], and one master holds [that] he is associating [it] with [its] permitted [state] after the sprinkling of the blood.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:2:1.hebrew: אמר קרא כי ידור נדר, כי ידור בדבר הנדור - הוי נדר ואסור, לאפוקי בכור דדבר האסור, דממילא מיתסר:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:2:1.english: The verse states: “When [a man] vows a vow” — [meaning,] when he vows by an item forbidden by a vow - it is [a valid] vow and is forbidden; to the exclusion of a firstborn, which is a forbidden item, as it becomes forbidden on its own.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:3:1.hebrew: אמר קרא לה' לרבות דבר האסור - דכל דבר שהוא אסור ולגבוה הוא, מתפיסו נמי בנדר אע"פ שהוא אסור בלא נדר, כגון בכור:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:3:1.english: The verse states: "To the Lord," to include an item that is forbidden - For anything that is forbidden and is [consecrated] to the Most High, one also associates [another object] with it in a vow, even though it is forbidden without a vow, such as a firstborn [animal].

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:5:1.hebrew: מרבה אני חטאת ואשם - שהם מתפיסים, מפני שהוא מתפיסן בנדר. אע"ג דעל חטא באין ולא משום נדר, אפ"ה איהו מתפיסו, שאומר: "הרי זו לחטאתי ולאשמי". אבל בכור אינו מתפיס כלל, שממעי אמו קדש עצמו:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:5:1.english: I include a sin-offering and a guilt-offering - For they are [valid objects for] associating [a vow], because he associates them by a vow. Even though they come for a sin and not because of a vow, nevertheless he is the one who designates it, as he says: "Behold, this is for my sin-offering [or] for my guilt-offering." However, a firstborn he does not designate at all, for from its mother's womb it became sanctified on its own.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:7:1.hebrew: כי לא מקדיש ליה - אם לא הקדישו, מי לא מיקדיש בלאו הכי? משום הכי לא חשיב כלל כי מתפיס ליה בנדר. אבל חטאת ואשם לא מיקדשי לעולם אי לא מקדיש להו:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:7:1.english: If he does not consecrate it - If he did not consecrate it, is it not consecrated even without that? Therefore, it is not considered [anything] at all when he links [something] to it in a vow. However, a sin-offering and a guilt-offering are never consecrated if he does not consecrate them.

Rashi on Nedarim 13a:9:1.hebrew: כולן שאוכל לך אסור - דכי אמר כאימרא שאוכל לך, דמי כמאן דאמר יאסר עלי מה שאוכל לך. אבל אמר כאימרא לא אוכל לך, מותר, דמשמע אבל אם אוכל לך לא יהא כאימרא, ומותר:
Rashi on Nedarim 13a:9:1.english: All of them, "that which I will eat of yours," it is forbidden - For when he says, "Like a lamb, that which I will eat of yours," it is as though he said, "May whatever I eat of yours be forbidden to me." But [if] he said, "Like a lamb, [that which] I will not eat of yours," it is permitted, because it implies, "but if I eat of yours, it shall not be like a lamb," and [thus] it is permitted.

Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:13:1.hebrew: האומר קרבן עולה ומנחה וכו' - אשמעי' אע"ג דליכא כ"ף:
Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:13:1.english: "One who says: An offering, a burnt-offering, a meal-offering, etc." - [The Mishnah] teaches us [that it is forbidden] even though there is no kaf [prefixed].

Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:13:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה מתיר - משום דלא אמר בכ"ף. וה"ה בלשון קונם בלא כ"ף דמותר טפי, דלא עדיף מלשון קרבן עצמו. וקונם בכל הש"ס בלא כ"ף — דלא כרבי יהודה. ור"י פי' דאמר קונם, יש לפרש לשון פעולה כמו "מקונם", ובלשון פעולה מודה רבי יהודה, כקרבן הקרבן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:13:2.english: Rabbi Yehuda renders [it] permitted - Because he did not say [it] with a kaf [i.e., "like an offering"]. And the same applies to the expression konam without a kaf, that it is even more [clearly] permitted, for it is no stronger than the expression "an offering" itself. And [the usage of] konam throughout the entire Talmud without a kaf is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda. And Ri explained that [when] one says konam, it can be interpreted as a verbal form, like mekonam ["rendered konam"], and with a verbal form Rabbi Yehuda concedes [that it is forbidden], like [the cases of] "kekorban" [and] "hakorban":

Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:13:3.hebrew: הקרבן כקרבן קרבן אוכל לך אסור - תימה: בשלמא "הקרבן" אשמעינן דלא "הא קרבן" קאמר, כיון שאמר "הקרבן" תיבה אחת; אבל אינך תרתי למה לי? ואי משום "קרבן" בלא כ"ף, כבר אשמעינן! (ונראה דא"ל) דוקא "שאוכל לך" הוא דאסור, אבל "לא אוכל לך" מותר, דלא מפרש: קרבן יהא, לפיכך לא אוכל לך. כך נראה למהר"ף נ"ע:
Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:13:3.english: "Hakorban, kakorban, korban, [that which] I eat of yours, is forbidden" - This is puzzling! Granted, [the case of] hakorban ("the offering") teaches us that he is not saying ha korban ("this offering" [i.e., swearing by the life of the offering]), since he said hakorban as one word; but why do I need those other two [cases: kakorban ("like an offering") and korban ("an offering")]? And if [it is taught] because of korban without a kaf, [the Mishnah] already taught us [that earlier]! (And it seems [one can say]) [that] specifically "[that] I will eat of yours" is forbidden, whereas "I will not eat of yours" is permitted, because it is not interpreted [as]: "May it be an offering, therefore I will not eat of yours." Thus it appears to our teacher, Rabbi Peretz, may his rest be in Eden.

Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:3:1.hebrew: אמר קרא לה' לרבות דבר האסור - פי': דבר האסור כי האי דבכור, לפי שנחשב קצת דבר הנדור, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:3:1.english: The verse states: “To the Lord,” to include an item that is forbidden - Explanation: [It refers to] a forbidden item such as this [case] of a firstborn [animal], because it is considered somewhat of a vowed item, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain.

Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:5:1.hebrew: מרבה אני חטאת ואשם שהוא מתפיס בנדר - אע"ג שהוא חייב אותן בלא נדר, מ"מ אין קדושה חל עליהן ממילא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:5:1.english: I include the sin-offering and guilt-offering, that he associates [the object of his vow] by means of a vow - Even though he is obligated [to bring] them without a vow, nevertheless sanctity does not take effect upon them automatically.

Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:9:1.hebrew: תנא אימרא לאימרא וכו' הא דאמר לאימרא - בפתח, דלאימרא בפתח מפרשינן ליה: לאימרא יהא, לפיכך לא אוכל לך, כמו לקרבן בפתח. והא דתניא בהך ברייתא: לאימרא לא אוכל לך מותר, מיירי שאמר לא אימרא, כפר"ת. וא"ת: אי לאימרא דהך ברייתא מיירי דאמר לא אימרא, אם כן "שאוכל לך" אמאי משמע איסורא? וי"ל: דודאי לאימרא דרישא (דלא) ד"אוכל לך" מיירי בלאימרא בפתח, ולאימרא ד"לא אוכל" מיירי שאמר לא אימרא. וא"ת: אם כן, אדמפליג ב"לא אימרא" בין "אוכל" ל"לא אוכל", ליפלוג כולה ב"לא אוכל" בין לאימרא בפתח ללא אימרא! דהשתא נמי דמפליג בין "אוכל" ל"לא אוכל", הוי לאימרא גבי "אוכל" בפתח, וגבי "לא אוכל" — לא אימרא! וי"ל: דאה"נ; אלא כיון דאימרא כאימרא לא ליתני ליה לאיסורא רק ב"אוכל לך", תני נמי ב"אוכל לך" גבי לאימרא, ואע"ג דגבי לאימרא הוי מתסר נמי גם ב"לא אוכל לך". כך צריך לדחוק לפר"ת. ור"י גרס: הא דאמר לאימרא — בחטף; התם מפרש ליה: לאימרא יהא, לפיכך לא אוכל לך, דומיא דלקרבן לא אוכל לך, דהתם נמי לקרבן בחטף. הא ברייתא דלעיל דשרי, מיירי בלאימרא בפתח, בין ברישא גבי "שאוכל" בין גבי "לא אוכל לך":
Tosafot on Nedarim 13a:9:1.english: It was taught [in a baraita]: "Imra, le'imra," etc. "This [refers to a case] where he said le'imra" - [This is vocalized] with a patach [i.e., la'imra], because we interpret la'imra with a patach as: "To a lamb shall it be; therefore, I will not eat of yours," just like lakorban with a patach. And that which is taught in this baraita, "Le'imra, I will not eat of yours — it is permitted," speaks of [a case] where he said "lo imra" ["not a lamb"], in accordance with the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam. And if you ask: If "le'imra" of this baraita speaks of [a case] where he said "lo imra," if so, [when he says] "that which I will eat of yours," why does it imply a prohibition? One can answer: Certainly "le'imra" of the first clause — [that] of "I will eat of yours" — speaks of "la'imra" with a patach, whereas "le'imra" of "I will not eat" speaks of [a case] where he said "lo imra." And if you ask: If so, instead of distinguishing in [the case of] "lo imra" between "I will eat" and "I will not eat," let it distinguish entirely in [the case of] "I will not eat" between "la'imra" with a patach and "lo imra"! For even now, when it distinguishes between "I will eat" and "I will not eat," "le'imra" with "I will eat" is with a patach, and with "I will not eat" it is "lo imra"! One can answer: Indeed, that is so; however, since [with regard to] "imra" [and] "ke'imra" [the tanna] could only teach the prohibition with "I will eat of yours," he also taught "I will eat of yours" with regard to "la'imra," even though with regard to "la'imra" it would also be forbidden even with "I will not eat of yours." Thus one is forced to explain according to Rabbeinu Tam's explanation. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak reads the text: "This [refers to a case] where he said le'imra" — with a chataf [sheva]; there one interprets it [as]: "For a lamb shall it be; therefore, I will not eat of yours," similar to "lekorban, I will not eat of yours," for there too "lekorban" is with a chataf. [Whereas] this baraita above that permits [it] speaks of "la'imra" with a patach, both in the first clause regarding "that which I will eat" and regarding "I will not eat of yours."
